sections.overview: Molossus sinaloae is a free-tailed bat whose current range records are centred in Mexico; recent taxonomic revisions narrowed a range once reported across Central and northern South America.
sections.identification: It is a medium-sized member of the mastiff-bat family Molossidae; field identification can be difficult among similar Molossus species.
sections.habitat: In Mexico it has been recorded in varied settings, including the Pacific coastal plain; older accounts also describe use of both dry and wet forests.
sections.diet: It catches flying insects in open air; moths and beetles are among reported prey.
sections.behavior: Like other free-tailed bats, it roosts by day in sheltered cavities; historic records include building roosts, sometimes with dozens of bats.
sections.reproduction: Available accounts report reproduction in Mexico, but timing and colony patterns are not well established across its revised range.
sections.ecology: The name reflects its type locality in Sinaloa. Older Central American records need care because similar Molossus bats were later separated or re-identified.
sections.conservation: The Mammal Diversity Database lists it as Least Concern, but the restricted range shown by current taxonomic treatments differs from older assessments and merits updated monitoring.
